_doc: Generated-only replacement placement spec. Heading anchors were retained from the original reviewed placement file.

figures.alt: Bathroom vanity placed before the countertop with drain and supply access visible
figures.caption: Confirm wall backing, level, plumbing locations, and door clearances before the countertop goes on. The cabinet needs to stay secure while leaving room to service the plumbing.

figures.alt: Vanity cabinet with accessible sink P-trap and supply valves
figures.caption: Reconnect the drain and supplies without forcing their alignment. Accessible shutoffs and a correctly assembled trap make future service far less disruptive.

figures.alt: Bathroom sink drain body and pop-up linkage inside a vanity cabinet
figures.caption: Test the drain, overflow, and pop-up before loading the cabinet. A slow leak is easier to find while the interior is empty and all connection points remain visible.
